subject: Console route inventory + dependency map for per-route cost/latency work
thread_summary: Request to create a canonical per-route inventory and dependency map to power a new console view for cost/latency attribution. Includes specs, priority asks, and infra feasibility notes.

> Thanks Sam — this is helpful. I'm looping in product and infra at Redwood to make sure we have a canonical route inventory and dependency map. We want a console view that:

From: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Cc: Sam Green <sam.green@acme.ai>
Date: Fri, 15 Mar 2024 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Console route inventory + dependency map for per-route cost/latency work

Hi team —

Following Sam's sample, asking us to build the baseline inventory + dependency map that the Console team can use to power a per-route economics view. High-level asks:

1) Output CSV/drive folder with the following columns (example attached): route, method, internal_subroute, model_family, model_variant(s), primary_region, avg_tokens_7d, cost_7d_usd, median_p95_latency_ms_7d, cacheable_prefixes (comma-separated), kv_cache_hit_rate_pct, owner

2) A dependency graph (PNG/SVG) that shows which microservices or internal routing layers typically invoke each route (we can pull traces). This should allow the Console to show a "call chain" and attribute upstream costs.

3) Priorities: start with high-volume public routes (top 50 by tokens/week), then expand. We need a clear owner column so Console can link to team pages.

Constraints / questions for infra:
- How expensive is it to compute kv_cache_hit_rate_pct for historical windows?
- Can we export model_variant mapping reliably for canary/pinned versions?

I've attached a tiny starter CSV (route_inventory.csv) and a rough dependency sketch. Can Marcus and Jasmine confirm feasibility and an ETA? Grace, can you prioritise whether this lands in the April Console sprint or later?

Thanks,
Diego
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

--- Attachment: route_inventory.csv (stub)
--- Attachment: dependency_graph.png (stub)

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai, jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 18 Mar 2024 14:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Console route inventory + dependency map for per-route cost/latency work

Diego / team —

We can produce the CSV and a dependency graph but want to call out a few implementation/ops tradeoffs:

- kv_cache_hit_rate_pct: we only have per-token cache instrumentation for active serving nodes. For a historical 30d window we'd need a nightly aggregation job that scans request logs and KV-cache events. Estimated infra effort: 2-3 engineer-days + small infra cost for aggregation (storage/compute).

- model_variant mapping: we have a runtime table that maps route -> active model variants per deployment. We can snapshot that, but for rollouts you'll get multiple variants per route; we'll include an array field in the CSV.

- call chain: tracing data is available, but sampling is aggressive for low-volume routes. For a high-quality dependency graph we should start with top-50 routes and increase sampling for 2 weeks. That will add pressure to our tracing ingest.

Proposed plan:
1) Deliver an initial CSV for top-50 routes (ETA: 6 business days).
2) Produce a draft dependency graph using sampled traces (ETA: +3 business days).
3) Add nightly aggregation for kv cache metrics (ETA: +2 sprints if we need 30d rolling accuracy).

I'll open OBS-4821 and drop a PR template for the Console team to consume (CSV schema + example).

-Marcus
Principal SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 18 Mar 2024 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Console route inventory + dependency map for per-route cost/latency work

Thanks all — this looks good and aligned with product goals. A few follow-ups / decisions:

- Prioritization: put this in the April Console sprint but scope to top-50 routes for the first pass. If Marcus' ETA holds, that should be fine.
- UX: Jasmine, please prepare a quick mock of the console card that can consume the CSV. Focus on: 1) per-route quick stats (7d cost, p95), 2) button to drill into call chain, and 3) a flag indicating cacheable prefixes. We may want to allow an "export owner" and "create ticket" quick action.
- Compliance: Diego, please coordinate with security if any trace data we pull needs redaction before sharing externally (Sam is cc'd; we'll mark any export PII-free).

Let's treat the kv-cache historical metric as stretch scope for the first sprint; include a TODO in the PR. Marcus — please post OBS-4821 link when ready and assign to Console eng leads.

Grace O'Connor
Product Manager, Console
Redwood Inference
